mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each week for the last three weeks (-45.6 to -36.7), a monotonic recovery trend that mechanically extrapolates forward as reopening momentum continues to pull retail footfall upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased monotonically from -45.6 to -36.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days despite the prior monotonic three-week rise.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in TRANSIT (from -40.3 to -33.0, +7.3 points) indicates restored commuter and errand travel capacity, which within one week feeds through to increased retail visitation as transit-dependent shoppers resume trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -40.3 to -33.0 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a TRANSIT jump exceeding 5 points, observed across repeated instances.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility jumped from near-zero to positive territory (0.1 to 0.7) after being deeply negative three weeks prior, signaling a policy relaxation of outdoor gathering restrictions; such relaxation events are typically paired with retail reopening, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive baseline deviation
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -14.9 at t-3w to +0.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite PARKS having crossed into positive territory in the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has been steadily declining (11.0 to 8.7) while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative and volatile (-49.0 to -44.3 with a dip to -50.9); the combination of falling residential confinement and stagnant-to-worsening workplace attendance implies households are substituting discretionary outings for commuting, which together drive a short-term rise in retail visits.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for 3+ consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES stays below -40
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.0 to 8.7 over four weeks while WORKPLACES stayed between -44.3 and -50.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks when RESIDENTIAL falls for three or more consecutive weeks under persistently negative WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved sharply over four weeks (-21.7 to -11.3), outpacing RETAIL_REC's recovery rate; since grocery/pharmacy trips typically lead broader discretionary retail recovery by one to two weeks as essential-trip normalization precedes non-essential shopping, RETAIL_REC should rise further within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved by 10.4 points over four weeks, faster than RETAIL_REC's relative pace in the first two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks lags or reverses despite continued GROCERY_PHARM improvement.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES dropped sharply to -50.9 at t-1w before partially recovering to -44.3, suggesting a temporary tightening event (e.g., a restriction reimposition) that could presage a retail pullback if the tightening resumes; if WORKPLACES falls again below -50, expect RETAIL_REC to decline over the following four weeks as broader restrictions tighten.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -50 again within the next week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dipped to -50.9 at t-1w before recovering to -44.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next four weeks even if WORKPLACES falls below -50 again.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous strong recovery in PARKS (from -14.9 to +0.7) combined with easing TRANSIT declines suggests a seasonal shift (e.g., warmer weather) is pulling people outdoors and into mixed-use retail corridors; this seasonal effect interacting with transit normalization should compound to raise RETAIL_REC over four weeks beyond what either series would predict alone.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose by 15.6 points and TRANSIT rose by 10.4 points over the four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to show above-trend acceleration over four weeks even as both PARKS and TRANSIT continue improving jointly.

mechanism_narrative: The rate of RETAIL_REC improvement decelerated from +2.9 points (t-3w to t-2w) and +1.7 points (t-2w to t-1w) to +4.3 points in the latest week, an irregular acceleration; if this acceleration is a one-off rebound rather than sustained momentum, mean reversion will pull RETAIL_REC growth back down toward its prior slower pace within one week, producing a flat-to-negative four-week comparison once the rebound fades.
candidate_trigger: weekly RETAIL_REC gain exceeds 4 points after two prior weeks of smaller gains
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gains were 2.9, 1.7, then 4.3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to accelerate upward in the week following the large 4.3-point gain rather than reverting toward the prior slower pace.
